accepted.quote: Unfortunately, the bill focuses on protecting crude oil and refined petroleum pipelines in particular from the full scope of environmental reviews under the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) by narrowing the scope of Federal authorization to solely the first 1,000 feet of the pipeline after the border, and excluding consideration of the rest of the pipeline.
accepted.bill: H.R. 3062, the Promoting Cross-border Energy Infrastructure Act
accepted.rationale: Criticism of narrowing NEPA review to 1,000 feet indicates support for full-scope environmental review.

accepted.quote: The bill also severely curtails the power of DOE to condition and regulate the imports and exports of electricity to Canada and Mexico.
accepted.bill: H.R. 3062, the Promoting Cross-border Energy Infrastructure Act
accepted.rationale: Describing DOE conditioning authority as severely curtailed indicates support for retaining that regulatory authority.

accepted.quote: Given the correlation between domestic natural gas and electricity prices, this bill will likely lead to Americans paying more for power, heating, and cooking all at once.
accepted.bill: H.R. 3062, the Promoting Cross-border Energy Infrastructure Act
accepted.rationale: Warning that the bill will raise household energy costs indicates opposition to expanded LNG export facilitation.
